Package com.google.mu.protobuf.util

Class StructMaker

java.lang.Object
com.google.mu.protobuf.util.StructMaker
@CheckReturnValue public class StructMaker extends Object
A helper class that makes it easier to create Struct and Value instances off of POJO, without having to create intermediary Value wrappers.

For example, one can create a Struct literal as in: 


 Struct ironMan =
     new StructMaker()
         .struct("name", "Tony Stark", "age", 10, "titles", List.of("Iron Man", "Genius"));

For structs with even more fields, you can use the toStruct() BiCollector, as in: 


 BiStream.of("k1", 1, "k2", 2, "k3", 3, "k4", 4, ...)
     .collect(new StructMaker().toStruct());
Or, create a Struct off of a Map: 

 new StructMaker()
     .struct(Map.of("k1", 1, "k2", 2, "k3", 3, "k4", 4, ...));

The toValue(java.lang.Object) method is responsible for converting POJO to Value, and recursively, the Collections, Maps and Tables thereof into corresponding ListValue or Struct wrappers.

For simple scenarios, prefer to use MoreStructs to create Struct. Its single-field struct() factory methods are more efficient, can be static imported, and will never throw IllegalArgumentException.

You can create a subclass to implement custom conversion logic. For example, if the application needs to convert User types to Value by using the user ids: 


 StructMaker maker = new StructMaker() {
   public Value toValue(Object obj) {
     if (obj instanceof User) {  // custom logic
       return convert(((User) obj).getId());
     }
     return super.toValue(obj);  // else delegate to default implementation
   }
 };

    • struct

      public final com.google.protobuf.Struct struct(CharSequence name, @Nullable Object value)
      Returns a Struct with name and value,with value converted using toValue(java.lang.Object). In particular, null is translated to NullValue.

      If runtime conversion error is undesirable, consider to use MoreStructs or build Struct manually with StructBuilder.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if value cannot be converted
      NullPointerException - if name is null

    • struct

      public final com.google.protobuf.Struct struct(CharSequence k1, @Nullable Object v1, CharSequence k2, @Nullable Object v2)
      Returns a Struct equivalent to {k1:v1, k2:v2}.

      Values are converted using toValue(java.lang.Object). In particular, null values are translated to NullValue.

      If runtime conversion error is undesirable, consider to use MoreStructs or build Struct manually with StructBuilder.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if duplicate keys are provided or if either value cannot be converted
      NullPointerException - if either key is null

    • nestedStruct

      public final com.google.protobuf.Struct nestedStruct(com.google.common.collect.Table<? extends CharSequence,? extends CharSequence,? extends @Nullable Object> table)
      Returns a nested Struct of Struct equivalent to the row map of table.

      Values are converted using toValue(java.lang.Object). In particular, null values are translated to NullValue.

      If runtime conversion error is undesirable, consider to use MoreStructs or build Struct manually with StructBuilder.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a Table cell value cannot be converted
      NullPointerException - if any row key or column key is null

    • toStruct

      public final BiCollector<CharSequence,@Nullable Object,com.google.protobuf.Struct> toStruct()
      Returns a BiCollector that accumulates the name-value pairs into a Struct with the values converted using toValue(java.lang.Object).

      Duplicate keys (according to CharSequence.toString()) are not allowed.

      Null keys are not allowed, but null values will be converted to NullValue.

      If runtime conversion error is undesirable, consider to use MoreStructs or build Struct manually with StructBuilder.

    • toValue

      public com.google.protobuf.Value toValue(@Nullable Object object)
      Converts object to Value. Must not return null.

      Supported types:

      • Primitive types (boolean, number, string)
      • null converted to NullValue
      • Enum encoded by name
      • Iterable and array elements recursively converted and wrapped in ListValuex
      • Map values recursively converted and wrapped in Struct
      • Multimap converted as convert(multimap.asMap())
      • Table converted as convert(table.rowMap())
      • Optional converted as convert(optional.orElse(null))
      • ImmutableIntArray, ImmutableLongArray and ImmutableDoubleArray elements wrapped in ListValue
      • Built-in protobuf types (Struct, Value, ListValue, NullValue)

    • defaultValue

      protected com.google.protobuf.Value defaultValue(Object object)
      Called by toValue(java.lang.Object) when object cannot be converted. Subclasses can override this method to throw a different exception type, or to return a catch-all default Value.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - to report that the type of object isn't supported
